newsitem.title: USA: Apple's Steven Jobs files to sell shrs-NYT.
newsitem.headline: Apple's Steven Jobs files to sell shrs-NYT.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc founder Steven Jobs has registered to sell all but one of the 1.5 million shares that he purchased when he sold Next Software to Apple in December, the New York Times said in Thursday's edition.
Jobs has recently been a part-time adviser to Apple from where he was ousted in 1985. After leaving Apple, he founded Next and Pixar Inc, a computer-animation studio.
Jobs said the filing was a routine matter executed on his behalf by Apple.
"I haven't sold any shares, and my intentions haven't changed at all," he said.
Nancy Paxton, the director of investor relations at Apple, said the filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission was a follow-up step related to its acquisition of Next for $400 million.
The stock issued to Jobs at that time were newly issued Apple shares. For those shares to have any value, they must be registered with the SEC at some point, Paxton said.
